PCI.BIO: Mohammad Refatul Islam is an Assistant Professor at the Department of Mechanical Engineering, University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV). Dr. Islam is also affiliated with the Material Science and Engineering, and Biomedical Engineering programs at UTRGV. His research interests broadly focuses on the fascinating interplay between microstructure and mechanics in biological and biomimetic materials. The overarching vision is to identify microstructural cues of soft tissue diseases and develop bioinspired materials for mechanical and biomedical engineering applications. Prior to joining UTRGV, Professor Islam was an NIH T32 Fellow at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Equipment: MRI: Track 1 Acquisition of Polytec MSA-600 Micro System Analyzer for Biomedical Engineering
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: Requested Instrument: Polytec MSA-600-X/U Micro System Analyzer ($695,790), state-of-the-art instrument crucial for biomedical engineering research and education the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV). The location of the instrument is the BIO-MEMS Laboratory (Director Caruntu). Servingover 34,000 students, UTRGV is a non-PhD-granting, minority-serving institution with a predominantly Hispanic student body (92%). The university aims to become an emerging research institution and establish a strong biomedical engineering community. This advanced equipment is crucial to preparing students in engineering, science, and medicine by providing hands-on research experiences that can lead to graduate studies, academic roles, or leadership positions in industry. UTRGV is experiencing rapid growth, with increasing student enrollment and the hiring of new faculty. A recently formed Biomedical Engineering(BME) Cluster for research and education includes eight faculty members, four of whom were hired within the past two years. Supporting faculty research development depends on access to cutting-edge infrastructure like the requested analyzer. Securing this grant lays a foundation for attracting external funding and fostering multidisciplinary collaborations. The lack of this instrument currently limits research efforts. This proposal is strongly supported by UTRGV administration, aligning with the university’s strategic goal of building a robust biomedical engineering research and education program.

CONGRANT.TITLE: MRI: Track 1 Acquisition of a Photo-Induced Force Microscope for Simultaneous Nanoscopic and Spectroscopic Imaging of Multifunctional Materials and Interfaces
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: The main goal of this proposal is to acquire cutting-edge Photo Induced Force Microscopy (PiFM) to enable new research and foster interdisciplinary research in nanotechnology, advanced manufacturing, biomedical, and applied physics education programs in the Rio Grande Valley, South Texas region. The overall objective is to expand and enhance the research infrastructure and capacity to conduct cutting-edge research projects at the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV), thereby increasing the number of students and well-trained, experienced investigators conducting material, manufacturing, and biophysical research at the nanoscale.

CONGRANT.TITLE: REU SITE: Interdisciplinary Research Experience for Undergraduates in Materials Science and Engineering at UTRGV
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: This REU Site award to the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV) will support the training of diverse undergraduate students in cutting edge research for 10 weeks during the summers of 2025-2027. A total of 30 students will be supported by the REU site in a three-year comprehensive engineering research activity. The students will be exposed to hands-on learning experience in the basics of materials science and engineering, involved in cutting-edge multidisciplinary research activities with aim to enrich their skills in the interrelationship between structure-processing-properties and performance of materials and nano/biomaterials. Exposure to these engineering research frontiers will arouse the students’ interest in pursuing higher education and considerably help increase both the number of students who choose engineering as their careers andthe education standards of UG students from minority and underrepresented groups across the USA. The REU site will also expand the knowledge and understanding of the technical projects by the students to develop and use diverse materials in real applications. The impact of this project will be already broadened by the direct participation of a HSI in engineering (UTRGV) as well as enhancing and maintaining an engineering-going (and a college-going) culture in a Hispanic- concentrated population. The REU site will also change the stereotypical gender and race assumptions in engineering and STEM study and career choice, especially for underrepresented Hispanic and women students. The proposed research activities will benefit society and national interest by advancing the existing knowledge in materials science and engineering and supporting diversity, research, and education at the national level.
